title: Traceable engineering change reports
author: Bijan Mousavi
why: Make fork proposals easy to review through evidence tied to each authored change, while preserving upstream ownership and application behavior.
what: Add fork contributor guidance, JSON validation, staged-payload fingerprints, escaped one-page PDF generation, report templates and focused regression tests.
how: Separate payload identity, validation and rendering. Test the exported staged payload, bind the record to its actual parent, and render escaped change descriptions into a readable one-page PDF.
preserved: All application source, public assets, dependencies, Node/Netlify configuration, chart interfaces and existing CI are byte-identical to the parent.
risk: Reports are fork-local evidence. Structure alone cannot prove claims. The inherited Docker context still includes developer files. No deployment change is included.
limitations: No remote CI, browser interaction or viewer decoding claim. Baseline npm audit reports 41 advisories, including two critical. No repository license declared. TeX Live 2024; Poppler 26.09.0.
rollback: Revert this coherent change with a new reported commit. Recheck application inputs against the parent and rerun relevant checks.

checks.command: git diff --cached --exit-code 'HEAD^' -- src public 'package*.json' '*.mjs' '*.toml' tsconfig.json Dockerfile helm-chart .github .dockerignore .vscode
